41.11.3 Estimation Methods
text:
Sun et al. (2025) propose two methods constructing common synthetic control:Concatenated Outcome Weights: Estimate weights minimizing imbalance across outcomes simultaneously:
\[
\hat{w} = \arg\min_w \sum_{k=1}^{K} || Y_{1,\text{pre},k} - \sum_{=2}^{N} w_i Y_{,\text{pre},k} ||^2
\]Concatenated Outcome Weights: Estimate weights minimizing imbalance across outcomes simultaneously:\[
\hat{w} = \arg\min_w \sum_{k=1}^{K} || Y_{1,\text{pre},k} - \sum_{=2}^{N} w_i Y_{,\text{pre},k} ||^2
\]Averaged Outcome Weights: Estimate weights based linear combination (e.g., average) outcomes:
\[
\hat{w} = \arg\min_w || \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} Y_{1,\text{pre},k} - \sum_{=2}^{N} w_i \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} Y_{,\text{pre},k} ||^2
\]Averaged Outcome Weights: Estimate weights based linear combination (e.g., average) outcomes:\[
\hat{w} = \arg\min_w || \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} Y_{1,\text{pre},k} - \sum_{=2}^{N} w_i \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} Y_{,\text{pre},k} ||^2
\]methods improve SCM performance reducing variance overfitting noise.

heading: 41.12.1 Synthetic Control Estimation
text: example simulates data 10 states 30 years, State receives treatment year 15. implement two approaches:Standard Synthetic Control using Synth.Generalized Synthetic Control using gsynth, incorporates iterative fixed effects multiple treated units.Load Required LibrariesWe construct panel dataset outcome variable \(Y\) influenced two covariates (\(X_1, X_2\)). Treatment (\(T\)) applied State year 15 onwards, artificial treatment effect +20.
code:
# install.packages("Synth")
# install.packages("gsynth")
library("Synth")
library("gsynth")
# Simulate panel data
set.seed(1)

df <- data.frame(
  year      = rep(1:30, 10),          # 30 years for 10 states
  state     = rep(LETTERS[1:10], each = 30),  # States A to J
  X1        = round(rnorm(300, 2, 1), 2),     # Continuous covariate
  X2        = round(rbinom(300, 1, 0.5) + rnorm(300), 2),  # Binary + noise
  state.num = rep(1:10, each = 30)    # Numeric identifier for states
)

# Outcome variable: Y = 1 + 2 * X1 + noise
df$Y <- round(1 + 2 * df$X1 + rnorm(300), 2)

# Assign treatment: Only State A (state == "A") from year 15 onward
df$T <- as.integer(df$state == "A" & df$year >= 15)

# Apply treatment effect: Increase Y by 20 where treatment is applied
df$Y[df$T == 1] <- df$Y[df$T == 1] + 20

# View data structure
str(df)

heading: 41.12.1.2 Modern alternatives: tidysynth and augsynth
text: classic Synth workflow relies building dataprep matrix predictors, treated/donor identifiers, time windows invoking synth(). Two recent packages streamline pipeline:tidysynth (Dunford) provides tidyverse-style API synthetic-control workflow expressed chained sequence verbs, synthetic_control() initializes object, generate_predictor() defines pre-treatment matching variables, generate_weights() solves donor weights, generate_control() constructs synthetic counterfactual. Diagnostics, plots, placebo tests dispatched resulting object via S3 methods (plot_trends(), plot_placebos(), grab_significance()), avoiding matrix bookkeeping required Synth::dataprep().augsynth (Ben-Michael, Feller, Rothstein), already used elsewhere chapter (see Section Augmented Synthetic Control Method), implements ridge-augmented synthetic control explicit bias correction recommended package pre-treatment fit poor.minimal tidysynth skeleton, parallel Synth example , :conceptual model identical Synth, convex combination donor units minimizes pre-treatment outcome (predictor) discrepancies, chained pipeline keeps data, weights, synthetic counterfactual bound single tibble-like object, convenient embedding inside dplyr/purrr workflows batch placebo inference.
code:
# install.packages("tidysynth")
library(tidysynth)
library(dplyr)

# `df` is a long-format panel with state, year, Y, X1, X2;
# state == "State A" is treated, intervention at year 15.
sc_out <- df %>%
    synthetic_control(
        outcome      = Y,
        unit         = state,
        time         = year,
        i_unit       = "State A",
        i_time       = 15,
        generate_placebos = TRUE
    ) %>%
    generate_predictor(
        time_window = 1:14,
        X1_mean     = mean(X1, na.rm = TRUE),
        X2_mean     = mean(X2, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    generate_weights(
        optimization_window = 1:14,
        margin_ipop         = 0.02,
        sigf_ipop           = 7,
        bound_ipop          = 6
    ) %>%
    generate_control()

sc_out %>% plot_trends()
sc_out %>% plot_placebos()
sc_out %>% grab_significance()
# See https://github.com/edunford/tidysynth for full examples.

heading: 41.12.3.3 Step 3: Fit the Micro-Synthetic Control Model
text: first estimate treatment effects using single follow-period.
code:
sea1 <- microsynth(
    seattledmi,
    idvar       = "ID",          # Unique unit identifier
    timevar     = "time",        # Time variable
    intvar      = "Intervention",# Treatment assignment
    start.pre   = 1,             # Start of pre-treatment period
    end.pre     = 12,            # End of pre-treatment period
    end.post    = 16,            # End of post-treatment period
    match.out   = match.out,     # Outcomes to match on
    match.covar = cov.var,       # Predictors to match on
    result.var  = match.out,     # Variables for treatment effect estimates
    omnibus.var = match.out,     # Variables for omnibus p-values
    test        = "lower",       # One-sided test (decrease in crime)
    n.cores     = min(parallel::detectCores() - 4, 2) # Parallel processing
)

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)


# Load dataset
df_leverage_effect <- read.csv("data/leverage_effect.csv.gz") %>%
    
    # Filter active firms
    filter(costat == "A") %>%
    
    # Drop missing values
    drop_na() %>%
    
    # Compute Shareholder Value (SHV)
    mutate(shv = prcc_f * csho) %>%
    
    # Compute Operating Business Value (OBV)
    mutate(obv = shv - ivst + dd1 + dltt + pstk) %>%
    
    # Compute Leverage Effect
    mutate(leverage_effect = obv / shv) %>%
    
    # Remove infinite values and non-positive leverage effects
    filter(is.finite(leverage_effect), leverage_effect > 0) %>%
    
    # Compute within-firm statistics
    group_by(gvkey) %>%
    mutate(
        within_mean_le = mean(leverage_effect, na.rm = TRUE),
        within_sd_le = sd(leverage_effect, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

# Summary statistics
mean_le <- mean(df_leverage_effect$leverage_effect, na.rm = TRUE)
max_le <- max(df_leverage_effect$leverage_effect, na.rm = TRUE)

# Plot histogram of leverage effect
hist(
    df_leverage_effect$leverage_effect,
    main = "Distribution of Leverage Effect",
    xlab = "Leverage Effect",
    col = "blue",
    breaks = 30
)

# Compute coefficient of variation (CV)
cv_le <-
    sd(df_leverage_effect$leverage_effect, na.rm = TRUE) / mean_le * 100

# Plot within-firm coefficient of variation histogram
df_leverage_effect %>%
    group_by(gvkey) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(cv = within_sd_le / within_mean_le) %>%
    pull(cv) %>%
    hist(
        main = "Within-Firm Coefficient of Variation",
        xlab = "CV",
        col = "red",
        breaks = 30
    )

# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse)

# Parameters
n                  <- 100000         # Number of observations
n_focal            <- round(n * 0.2) # Number of focal events
overlap_correlated <- 0.5            # Overlapping percentage between focal and correlated events

# Function to compute mean and confidence interval
mean_ci <- function(x) {
    m <- mean(x)
    ci <- qt(0.975, length(x)-1) * sd(x) / sqrt(length(x)) # 95% confidence interval
    list(mean = m, lower = m - ci, upper = m + ci)
}


# Simulate data
set.seed(42)
data <- tibble(
    date       = seq.Date(
        from = as.Date("2010-01-01"),
        by = "day",
        length.out = n
    ),
    # Date sequence
    focal      = rep(0, n),
    correlated = rep(0, n),
    ab_ret     = rnorm(n)
)


# Define focal events
focal_idx <- sample(1:n, n_focal)
data$focal[focal_idx] <- 1

true_effect <- 0.25

# Adjust the ab_ret for the focal events to have a mean of true_effect
data$ab_ret[focal_idx] <-
    data$ab_ret[focal_idx] - mean(data$ab_ret[focal_idx]) + true_effect



# Determine the number of correlated events that overlap with focal and those that don't
n_correlated_overlap <-
    round(length(focal_idx) * overlap_correlated)
n_correlated_non_overlap <- n_correlated_overlap

# Sample the overlapping correlated events from the focal indices
correlated_idx <- sample(focal_idx, size = n_correlated_overlap)

# Get the remaining indices that are not part of focal
remaining_idx <- setdiff(1:n, focal_idx)

# Check to ensure that we're not attempting to sample more than the available remaining indices
if (length(remaining_idx) < n_correlated_non_overlap) {
    stop("Not enough remaining indices for non-overlapping correlated events")
}

# Sample the non-overlapping correlated events from the remaining indices
correlated_non_focal_idx <-
    sample(remaining_idx, size = n_correlated_non_overlap)

# Combine the two to get all correlated indices
all_correlated_idx <- c(correlated_idx, correlated_non_focal_idx)

# Set the correlated events in the data
data$correlated[all_correlated_idx] <- 1


# Inflate the effect for correlated events to have a mean of
correlated_non_focal_idx <-
    setdiff(all_correlated_idx, focal_idx) # Fixing the selection of non-focal correlated events
data$ab_ret[correlated_non_focal_idx] <-
    data$ab_ret[correlated_non_focal_idx] - mean(data$ab_ret[correlated_non_focal_idx]) + 1


# Define the numbers of uncorrelated events for each scenario
num_uncorrelated <- c(5, 10, 20, 30, 40)

# Define uncorrelated events
for (num in num_uncorrelated) {
    for (i in 1:num) {
        data[paste0("uncorrelated_", i)] <- 0
        uncorrelated_idx <- sample(1:n, round(n * 0.1))
        data[uncorrelated_idx, paste0("uncorrelated_", i)] <- 1
    }
}


# Define uncorrelated columns and scenarios
unc_cols <- paste0("uncorrelated_", 1:num_uncorrelated)
results <- tibble(
    Scenario = c(
        "Include Correlated",
        "Correlated Effects",
        "Exclude Correlated",
        "Exclude Correlated and All Uncorrelated"
    ),
    MeanEffect = c(
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1])$mean,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 0 |
                                data$correlated == 1])$mean,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0])$mean,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0 &
                                rowSums(data[, paste0("uncorrelated_", 1:num_uncorrelated)]) == 0])$mean
    ),
    LowerCI = c(
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1])$lower,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 0 |
                                data$correlated == 1])$lower,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0])$lower,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0 &
                                rowSums(data[, paste0("uncorrelated_", 1:num_uncorrelated)]) == 0])$lower
    ),
    UpperCI = c(
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1])$upper,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 0 |
                                data$correlated == 1])$upper,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0])$upper,
        mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                data$correlated == 0 &
                                rowSums(data[, paste0("uncorrelated_", 1:num_uncorrelated)]) == 0])$upper
    )
)

# Add the scenarios for excluding 5, 10, 20, and 50 uncorrelated
for (num in num_uncorrelated) {
    unc_cols <- paste0("uncorrelated_", 1:num)
    results <- results %>%
        add_row(
            Scenario = paste("Exclude", num, "Uncorrelated"),
            MeanEffect = mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                                 data$correlated == 0 &
                                                 rowSums(data[, unc_cols]) == 0])$mean,
            LowerCI = mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                              data$correlated == 0 &
                                              rowSums(data[, unc_cols]) == 0])$lower,
            UpperCI = mean_ci(data$ab_ret[data$focal == 1 &
                                              data$correlated == 0 &
                                              rowSums(data[, unc_cols]) == 0])$upper
        )
}


ggplot(results,
       aes(
           x = factor(Scenario, levels = Scenario),
           y = MeanEffect,
           ymin = LowerCI,
           ymax = UpperCI
       )) +
    geom_pointrange() +
    coord_flip() +
    ylab("Mean Effect") +

library(tidyverse)

deals <- read.csv("data/car_bhar_replication.csv") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), announce_date = as.Date(announce_date))

# One row per firm-day: rel_day = 0 is the announcement's first trading day
# (Disney/Lucasfilm uses Oct 31, 2012, the first day markets reopened after
# Hurricane Sandy closed the NYSE on the announcement date itself).
c(n_deals = n_distinct(deals$deal), n_firm_days = nrow(deals))
#>     n_deals n_firm_days 
#>          19       19779
compute_deal <- function(sub) {
  est <- filter(sub, rel_day >= -260, rel_day <= -31)
  ev  <- filter(sub, rel_day >= -1,  rel_day <= 1)
  lr  <- filter(sub, rel_day >= 2,   rel_day <= 761)

  mm <- lm(ret_stock ~ ret_mkt, data = est)
  ar_event <- ev$ret_stock - predict(mm, newdata = ev)
  car <- sum(ar_event)

  stock_gross <- prod(1 + (exp(lr$ret_stock) - 1))
  mkt_gross   <- prod(1 + (exp(lr$ret_mkt) - 1))
  bhar <- stock_gross - mkt_gross

  tibble(CAR = car, BHAR = bhar, beta = coef(mm)[["ret_mkt"]])
}

results <- deals %>%
  group_by(deal) %>%
  group_modify(~ compute_deal(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(CAR))
ggplot(results, aes(CAR, BHAR)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "3-day announcement CAR", y = "3-year BHAR") +
  causalverse::ama_theme()#> Pearson correlation: 0.32 (95% CI -0.16 to 0.67, p = 0.18, n = 19)

code:
# Load necessary packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)


# Simulate stock returns and benchmark portfolio returns
set.seed(123)
months <- 60  # 5-year event window
firms <- 50   # Number of event firms

# Generate random stock returns (normally distributed)
stock_returns <-
    matrix(rnorm(months * firms, mean = 0.01, sd = 0.05),
           nrow = months,
           ncol = firms)

# Generate benchmark portfolio returns
benchmark_returns <- rnorm(months, mean = 0.009, sd = 0.03)

# Compute LCAR for each firm
LCARs <-
    apply(stock_returns, 2, function(stock)
        cumsum(stock - benchmark_returns))

# Convert to data frame for visualization
LCAR_df <- as.data.frame(LCARs) %>%
    mutate(Month = 1:months) %>%
    pivot_longer(-Month, names_to = "Firm", values_to = "LCAR")

# Plot LCAR trajectories
ggplot(LCAR_df, aes(x = Month, y = LCAR, group = Firm)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.3) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
        title = "Long-term Cumulative Abnormal Returns (LCARs)",
        x = "Months Since Event",
        y = "Cumulative Abnormal Return",
        caption = "Each line represents an event firm's LCAR trajectory."
    )

heading: 42.17.3 Worked Example with fixest
text:
fixest package implements event-study regression compactly () operator, expands categorical variable indicators chosen reference level. Fitting event study leads lags around treatment timing reduces one line.Prose reference: Fig. 42.8 plots dynamic coefficients TWFE event-study regression simulated staggered-adoption data.
Figure 42.8: Event-study coefficients two-way fixed-effects regression simulated staggered-adoption data, period treatment reference.
Two implementation details worth flagging. First, (ttt_bin, ref = -1) produces one indicator per unique value ttt_bin \(-1\), automatically following convention period immediately treatment reference. Second, clustering unit level (cluster = ~ id) handles within-unit serial correlation endemic panel event studies. Plot output can equivalently produced ggiplot::ggiplot(es_fit) ggplot2-based version easier customize.
code:
library(fixest)
library(data.table)

# Simulate a staggered-adoption panel.
set.seed(20260430)
n_units  <- 200
n_years  <- 20
years    <- 2001:(2000 + n_years)

# Treatment cohorts: 2008, 2012, 2016, plus a never-treated group.
cohort_pool <- c(2008, 2012, 2016, NA_integer_)
units       <- data.table(
    id = 1:n_units,
    g  = sample(cohort_pool, n_units, replace = TRUE)
)

panel <- CJ(id = units$id, year = years)
panel <- merge(panel, units, by = "id")

# Event time; never-treated coded as a large value so it is binned out.
panel[, time_to_treat := ifelse(is.na(g), 1000L, year - g)]
panel[, treated_post  := !is.na(g) & year >= g]

# Outcome: unit and year FEs plus a true dynamic effect that grows then plateaus.
true_effect <- function(k) ifelse(k < 0, 0, pmin(0.5 + 0.25 * k, 2.0))
panel[, unit_fe := rnorm(n_units)[id]]
panel[, year_fe := (year - 2000) * 0.05]
panel[, y := unit_fe + year_fe +
            ifelse(treated_post, true_effect(time_to_treat), 0) +
            rnorm(.N, sd = 0.5)]

# Bin the endpoints at -5 and +8 so the extremes don't drive the estimates.
panel[, ttt_bin := pmin(pmax(time_to_treat, -5L), 8L)]
panel[is.na(g), ttt_bin := -1L]   # never-treated absorbed into reference

es_fit <- feols(
    y ~ i(ttt_bin, ref = -1) | id + year,
    data    = panel,
    cluster = ~ id
)

iplot(
    es_fit,
    main      = "",
    xlab      = "Event time (years from treatment)",
    ylab      = "Estimated coefficient",
    ref.line  = -1,
    pt.join   = TRUE
)

heading: 43.3.1 Constant-Treatment-Effect Model
text:
constant treatment effect assumption (.e., treatment effect individuals),\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_{0i} &= \alpha + \eta_i, \\
Y_{1i} - Y_{0i} &= \rho, \\
Y_i &= Y_{0i} + D_i (Y_{1i} - Y_{0i}) \\
    &= \alpha + \eta_i  + D_i \rho \\
    &= \alpha + \rho D_i + \eta_i.
\end{aligned}

heading: 43.3.2 Instrumental Variable Solution
text:
valid instrument \(Z_i\) allows us estimate causal effect \(\rho\) via:\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho &= \frac{\text{Cov}(Y_i, Z_i)}{\text{Cov}(D_i, Z_i)} \\
     &= \frac{\text{Cov}(Y_i, Z_i) / V(Z_i) }{\text{Cov}(D_i, Z_i) / V(Z_i)} \\
     &= \frac{\text{Reduced form estimate}}{\text{First-stage estimate}} \\
     &= \frac{E[Y_i |Z_i = 1] - E[Y_i | Z_i = 0]}{E[D_i |Z_i = 1] - E[D_i | Z_i = 0 ]}.
\end{aligned}
\]ratio measures treatment effect \(Z_i\) valid instrument.

43.3.6.1 Common Pitfall: ITT Divided by the Wrong Complier Share
text:
common applied mistake compute “LATE = ITT / complier share” complier share replaced \(\Pr(D = 1 \mid Z = 1)\), .e. takeup rate treated assignment arm. correct \(\Pr(D = 1 \mid Z = 0) \approx 0\), meaning always-takers treatment uptake control assignment group. general,\[

\Pr(D = 1 \mid Z = 0) = \Pr(\text{always-taker}),
\]correct denominator first-stage difference \(\Pr(D = 1 \mid Z = 1) - \Pr(D = 1 \mid Z = 0)\). following simulation makes mistake visible: data-generating process always-takers, compliers, never-takers, treatment effect non-zero compliers.Wald ratio equals 2SLS coefficient design exactly identified controls. wrong denominator divides always-takers \(+\) compliers, produces smaller-magnitude estimate LATE.
code:
set.seed(12345)

simulate_binary_iv <- function(N = 20000,
                               p_complier = 0.40,
                               p_always   = 0.10,
                               tau_c      = 2.0,
                               sigma      = 1.0) {
    types <- sample(
        c("C", "A", "N"),
        size    = N,
        replace = TRUE,
        prob    = c(p_complier, p_always, 1 - p_complier - p_always)
    )
    Z  <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.5)
    D0 <- ifelse(types == "A", 1, 0)
    D1 <- ifelse(types %in% c("A", "C"), 1, 0)
    D  <- ifelse(Z == 1, D1, D0)
    U  <- rnorm(N)
    Y0 <- 1.0 + 1.5 * U + rnorm(N, sd = sigma)
    tau <- ifelse(types == "C", tau_c, 0.0)
    Y1  <- Y0 + tau
    Y   <- ifelse(D == 1, Y1, Y0)
    data.frame(Y, D, Z, type = types)
}

wald_late <- function(df) {
    ITT_Y <- mean(df$Y[df$Z == 1]) - mean(df$Y[df$Z == 0])
    FS    <- mean(df$D[df$Z == 1]) - mean(df$D[df$Z == 0])
    list(ITT_Y = ITT_Y, FS = FS, LATE = ITT_Y / FS)
}

df1 <- simulate_binary_iv()
w1  <- wald_late(df1)

# 2SLS with intercept only
stage1     <- lm(D ~ Z, data = df1)
df1$Dhat   <- fitted(stage1)
beta_2sls  <- coef(lm(Y ~ Dhat, data = df1))[["Dhat"]]

# Wrong "complier share" = Pr(D = 1 | Z = 1)
takeup_assigned <- mean(df1$D[df1$Z == 1])
late_wrong      <- w1$ITT_Y / takeup_assigned

data.frame(
    quantity = c(
        "ITT_Y",
        "First stage = E[D|Z=1] - E[D|Z=0]",
        "Wald LATE = ITT_Y / First stage",
        "2SLS coefficient",
        "Wrong denominator Pr(D = 1 | Z = 1)",
        "ITT_Y / Pr(D = 1 | Z = 1) (not LATE)"
    ),
    value = c(w1$ITT_Y, w1$FS, w1$LATE, beta_2sls,
              takeup_assigned, late_wrong)
)

\]tildes denote residuals partialling constant \(X\). clean way match 2SLS hand take ratio \(Z\) coefficient \(\mathrm{lm}(Y \sim Z + X)\) \(Z\) coefficient \(\mathrm{lm}(D \sim Z + X)\). simulation confirms :naive Wald biased \(Z\) correlated \(X\). 2SLS residualized Wald agree numerically.

simulate_with_covariate <- function(N = 30000,
                                    p_complier = 0.35,
                                    p_always   = 0.15,
                                    tau_c      = 2.0,
                                    sigma      = 1.0,
                                    z_strength = 0.8) {
    types <- sample(
        c("C", "A", "N"),
        size    = N,
        replace = TRUE,
        prob    = c(p_complier, p_always, 1 - p_complier - p_always)
    )
    X  <- rnorm(N)
    pZ <- 1 / (1 + exp(-z_strength * X))    # Z correlated with X
    Z  <- rbinom(N, 1, pZ)
    D0 <- ifelse(types == "A", 1, 0)
    D1 <- ifelse(types %in% c("A", "C"), 1, 0)
    D  <- ifelse(Z == 1, D1, D0)
    U  <- rnorm(N)
    Y0 <- 1.0 + 1.0 * X + 1.3 * U + rnorm(N, sd = sigma)
    tau <- ifelse(types == "C", tau_c, 0.0)
    Y   <- ifelse(D == 1, Y0 + tau, Y0)
    data.frame(Y, D, Z, X)
}

df2 <- simulate_with_covariate()
w2  <- wald_late(df2)               # naive Wald, ignores X

fs2 <- lm(D ~ Z + X, data = df2)
df2$Dhat   <- fitted(fs2)
beta_2sls_X <- coef(lm(Y ~ Dhat + X, data = df2))[["Dhat"]]

# Residualized Wald
residualize <- function(v, Xmat) {
    fit <- lm.fit(x = Xmat, y = v)
    v - Xmat %*% fit$coefficients
}
Xmat <- cbind(1, df2$X)
Ztil <- as.numeric(residualize(df2$Z, Xmat))
Ytil <- as.numeric(residualize(df2$Y, Xmat))
Dtil <- as.numeric(residualize(df2$D, Xmat))
beta_resid_wald <- mean(Ztil * Ytil) / mean(Ztil * Dtil)

data.frame(
    estimator = c(
        "Naive Wald using group means (no X)",
        "2SLS with X in both stages",
        "Residualized Wald after partialling out X"
    ),
    value = c(w2$LATE, beta_2sls_X, beta_resid_wald)
)
#>                                   estimator    value
#> 1       Naive Wald using group means (no X) 3.929947
#> 2                2SLS with X in both stages 1.908661
#> 3 Residualized Wald after partialling out X 1.908661

text:
Generalized Method Moments (GMM) provides flexible estimation framework generalizes Instrumental Variables (IV) approach, including 2SLS special case. key idea behind GMM use moment conditions derived economic models estimate parameters efficiently, even presence endogeneity.Consider standard linear regression model:\[
Y = X\beta + u, \quad u \sim (0, \Omega)

E[Z_i' u_i] = E[Z_i' (Y_i - X_i \beta)] = 0.
\]practice, expectations replaced sample analogs. empirical moment conditions given :\[
\bar{g}(\beta) = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{=1}^{N} Z_i' (Y_i - X_i \beta) = \frac{1}{N} Z' (Y - X\beta).
\]GMM estimates \(\beta\) minimizing quadratic function sample moments.

text:
Exactly Identified Case (\(l = k\))number instruments equals number endogenous regressors (\(l = k\)), moment conditions uniquely determine \(\beta\). case, IV estimator :\[
\hat{\beta}_{IV} = (Z'X)^{-1}Z'Y.
\]equivalent classical 2SLS estimator.Overidentified Case (\(l > k\))instruments endogenous variables (\(l > k\)), system moment conditions parameters. case, project \(X\) onto instrument space:\[
\hat{X} = Z(Z'Z)^{-1} Z' X = P_Z X.
\]2SLS estimator given :\[
\begin{aligned}
\hat{\beta}_{2SLS} &= (\hat{X}'X)^{-1} \hat{X}' Y \\
&= (X'P_Z X)^{-1} X' P_Z Y.
\end{aligned}
\]However, 2SLS optimally weight instruments \(l > k\). IV-GMM approach resolves issue.

\hat{\beta}_{GMM} = (X'ZWZ' X)^{-1} X'ZWZ'Y.

S = E[Z' u u' Z] = \lim_{N \\infty} N^{-1} [Z' \Omega Z].

# Load required packages
library(gmm)
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)  # For generalized inverse if needed

# General IV-GMM function with clustering
gmmcl <- function(formula, instruments, data, cluster_var, lambda = 1e-6) {
  
  # Ensure cluster_var exists in data
  if (!(cluster_var %in% colnames(data))) {
    stop("Error: Cluster variable not found in data.")
  }
  
  # Step 1: Initial GMM estimation (identity weighting matrix)
  initial_gmm <- gmm(formula, instruments, data = data, vcov = "TrueFixed", 
                      weightsMatrix = diag(ncol(model.matrix(instruments, data))))
  
  # Extract residuals
  u_hat <- residuals(initial_gmm)
  
  # Matrix of instruments
  Z <- model.matrix(instruments, data)
  
  # Ensure clusters are treated as a factor
  data[[cluster_var]] <- as.factor(data[[cluster_var]])
  
  # Compute clustered weighting matrix
  cluster_groups <- split(seq_along(u_hat), data[[cluster_var]])
  
  # Remove empty clusters (if any)
  cluster_groups <- cluster_groups[lengths(cluster_groups) > 0]
  
  # Initialize cluster-based covariance matrix
  S_cluster <- matrix(0, ncol(Z), ncol(Z))  # Zero matrix
  
  # Compute clustered weight matrix
  for (indices in cluster_groups) {
    if (length(indices) > 0) {  # Ensure valid clusters
      u_cluster <- matrix(u_hat[indices], ncol = 1)  # Convert to column matrix
      Z_cluster <- Z[indices, , drop = FALSE]        # Keep matrix form
      S_cluster <- S_cluster + t(Z_cluster) %*% (u_cluster %*% t(u_cluster)) %*% Z_cluster
    }
  }
  
  # Normalize by sample size
  S_cluster <- S_cluster / nrow(data)
  
  # Ensure S_cluster is invertible
  S_cluster <- S_cluster + lambda * diag(ncol(S_cluster))  # Regularization

  # Compute inverse or generalized inverse if needed
  if (qr(S_cluster)$rank < ncol(S_cluster)) {
    S_cluster_inv <- ginv(S_cluster)  # Use generalized inverse (MASS package)
  } else {
    S_cluster_inv <- solve(S_cluster)
  }

  # Step 2: GMM estimation using clustered weighting matrix
  final_gmm <- gmm(formula, instruments, data = data, vcov = "TrueFixed", 
                    weightsMatrix = S_cluster_inv)
  
  return(final_gmm)
}

)

library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(Matrix)
setFixest_notes(FALSE)
set.seed(20261001)

ph_mu    <- -4.5   # true effect of the 12-month log price change on the log hazard
ph_rho   <-  3.0   # omitted local default risk = ph_rho x local price shock
ph_gamma <- c(`2003` = 0, `2004` = 0.05, `2005` = 0.15, `2006` = 0.10, `2007` = 0.05)

# Housing markets: 50 CBSAs; calendar month 1 = Jan 2003, 120 = Dec 2012
ph_G   <- 50
ph_nat <- function(s)   # national log price factor: boom to mid-2006, bust to mid-2009
    ifelse(s <= 42, 0.10 * s / 12, 0.10 * 42 / 12 - 0.13 * (pmin(s, 78) - 42) / 12)
ph_cbsa <- data.table(g = 1:ph_G, sigma = exp(rnorm(ph_G, 0, 0.35)))  # past cyclicality
# Time-invariant market risk correlated with cyclicality: absorbed by market FE
ph_cbsa[, alpha_g := 0.3 * as.numeric(scale(sigma)) + rnorm(ph_G, 0, 0.2)]
ph_ar1 <- function(n, phi = 0.9, sd = 0.10) {
    x <- numeric(n); x[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, sd)
    e <- rnorm(n, 0, sd * sqrt(1 - phi^2))
    for (k in 2:n) x[k] <- phi * x[k - 1] + e[k]
    x
}
ph_mk <- CJ(g = 1:ph_G, s = -11:120)[ph_cbsa, on = "g"]
setorder(ph_mk, g, s)
ph_mk[, v := ph_ar1(.N), by = g]                       # local price shock
ph_mk[, z := sigma * (ph_nat(s) - ph_nat(s - 12))]      # instrument
ph_mk[, dp := z + v]                                    # 12-month change in log prices
ph_mk[, omega := ph_rho * v]                            # omitted local default risk

# Loans: five annual cohorts, followed monthly for up to 60 months
ph_N  <- 20000
ph_ln <- data.table(id = 1:ph_N, cohort = rep(2003:2007, each = ph_N / 5))
ph_ln[, orig := (cohort - 2003) * 12 + sample(0:11, .N, TRUE)]
ph_ln[, g    := sample.int(ph_G, .N, TRUE)]
ph_ln[, fico := rnorm(.N)]                                   # standardized credit score
ph_ln[, cltv := rnorm(.N, mean = 0.15 * (cohort - 2003) / 4)] # leverage drifts up
ph_ln[, gam  := ph_gamma[as.character(cohort)]]

ph_pp <- ph_ln[, .(age = 1:60), by = id][ph_ln, on = "id"]
ph_pp[, s := orig + age]
ph_pp <- ph_mk[, .(g, s, alpha_g, z, dp, v, omega)][ph_pp, on = .(g, s)]
setorder(ph_pp, id, age)

ph_psi <- function(a) log(0.002 + 0.010 * (a / 24) * exp(1 - a / 24))  # hump-shaped baseline
ph_h   <- function(eta) -expm1(-exp(eta))                               # grouped-time hazard
ph_pp[, eta_d := ph_psi(age) + gam - 0.4 * fico + 0.3 * cltv + alpha_g + ph_mu * dp + omega]
ph_pp[, eta_p := log(0.02) + 3 * dp + 0.2 * fico - 0.15 * cltv]          # prepayment
ph_pp[, ev := fifelse(runif(.N) < ph_h(eta_d), 1L,
                      fifelse(runif(.N) < ph_h(eta_p), 2L, 0L))]
ph_pp[, last := { w <- which(ev > 0L); if (length(w)) w[1] else .N }, by = id]
ph_est <- ph_pp[age <= last]                                 # observed loan-months
ph_est[, default := as.integer(ev == 1L & age == last)]
ph_est[, prepay  := as.integer(ev == 2L & age == last)]

c(loans = ph_N, loan_months = nrow(ph_est),
  defaults = sum(ph_est$default), prepayments = sum(ph_est$prepay))
#>       loans loan_months    defaults prepayments 
#>       20000      497675        6803       10794
ph_rhs <- "fico + cltv + i(cohort, ref = 2003)"
ph_fe  <- "| age + g"                        # nonparametric baseline + market FE
ph_fam <- binomial("cloglog")

# First stage with the same controls as the hazard
ph_fs <- feols(as.formula(paste("dp ~ z +", ph_rhs, ph_fe)), ph_est, cluster = ~g)
ph_est[, vhat := resid(ph_fs)]

ph_naive <- feglm(as.formula(paste("default ~ dp +", ph_rhs, ph_fe)), ph_est,
                  family = ph_fam, cluster = ~g)
ph_cf    <- feglm(as.formula(paste("default ~ dp + vhat +", ph_rhs, ph_fe)), ph_est,
                  family = ph_fam, cluster = ~g)
ph_cf3   <- feglm(as.formula(paste("default ~ dp + vhat + I(vhat^2) + I(vhat^3) +",
                                   ph_rhs, ph_fe)),
                  ph_est, family = ph_fam, cluster = ~g)

# Two-step GMM variance: stack the first-stage OLS moments and the cloglog
# score moments, sum within markets, and use the expected Hessian.
ph_W1  <- sparse.model.matrix(~ z + fico + cltv + factor(cohort) + factor(age) +
                                  factor(g), ph_est)
ph_W2  <- sparse.model.matrix(~ dp + vhat + fico + cltv + factor(cohort) + factor(age) +
                                  factor(g), ph_est)
ph_eta <- predict(ph_cf, type = "link")
ph_m   <- ph_fam$linkinv(ph_eta)
ph_me  <- ph_fam$mu.eta(ph_eta)
ph_w   <- ph_me^2 / ph_fam$variance(ph_m)                       # information weights
ph_sc  <- (ph_est$default - ph_m) * ph_me / ph_fam$variance(ph_m) # score in the index
ph_Hi  <- solve(crossprod(ph_W2, ph_W2 * ph_w))
ph_M   <- crossprod(ph_W2, ph_W1 * ph_w) %*% solve(crossprod(ph_W1))
ph_C   <- sparseMatrix(i = ph_est$g, j = seq_len(nrow(ph_est)), x = 1)  # market sums
ph_S2  <- ph_C %*% (ph_W2 * ph_sc)
ph_S1  <- ph_C %*% (ph_W1 * ph_est$vhat)
ph_adj <- (ph_G / (ph_G - 1)) * ((nrow(ph_est) - 1) / (nrow(ph_est) - ncol(ph_W2)))
ph_A   <- ph_S2 + coef(ph_cf)[["vhat"]] * ph_S1 %*% t(ph_M)
ph_se_gmm <- sqrt(diag(as.matrix(ph_adj * ph_Hi %*% crossprod(ph_A) %*% ph_Hi)))[2:3]

options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Model = c("Naive cloglog hazard", "Control function, linear c(v)",
              "Control function, cubic c(v)", "Truth"),
    `Price coefficient` = c(coef(ph_naive)[["dp"]], coef(ph_cf)[["dp"]],
                            coef(ph_cf3)[["dp"]], ph_mu),
    `SE, second stage only` = c(se(ph_naive)[["dp"]], se(ph_cf)[["dp"]],
                                se(ph_cf3)[["dp"]], NA),
    `SE, two-step GMM` = c(NA, ph_se_gmm[1], NA, NA),
    `Residual coefficient` = c(NA, coef(ph_cf)[["vhat"]], coef(ph_cf3)[["vhat"]], ph_rho),
    `Residual SE, two-step GMM` = c(NA, ph_se_gmm[2], NA, NA),
    check.names = FALSE
), digits = 3,
caption = "Default hazard estimates on simulated loan-month data. The price coefficient is the effect of the 12-month change in log local house prices on the log hazard. Standard errors are clustered by market.")
# Effect of a 10 percent price decline on the average monthly default hazard,
# holding the control function (or, for the truth, the omitted factor) fixed
ph_asf <- function(eta, slope) mean(ph_h(eta - 0.10 * slope)) / mean(ph_h(eta)) - 1
ph_decline <- c(Truth = ph_asf(ph_est$eta_d, ph_mu),
                `Naive hazard` = ph_asf(predict(ph_naive, type = "link"), coef(ph_naive)[["dp"]]),
                `Control function` = ph_asf(predict(ph_cf, type = "link"), coef(ph_cf)[["dp"]]))

# Five-year cumulative default by cohort under actual and common price paths
ph_prep <- feglm(as.formula(paste("prepay ~ dp +", ph_rhs, ph_fe)),
                 ph_est[default == 0L], family = ph_fam)
ph_pp[, vhat := dp - predict(ph_fs, newdata = ph_pp)]
ph_cif60 <- function(eta_d, eta_p, id) {
    dt <- data.table(id, hd = ph_h(eta_d), hp = ph_h(eta_p))
    dt[, S_prev := shift(cumprod((1 - hd) * (1 - hp)), fill = 1), by = id]
    dt[, .(cif = sum(hd * S_prev)), by = id]$cif
}
ph_scen <- list(`Actual prices` = NULL, `All cohorts face 2003 cohort's prices` = 2003,
                `All cohorts face 2006 cohort's prices` = 2006)
ph_out <- rbindlist(lapply(names(ph_scen), function(nm) {
    d <- copy(ph_pp)
    if (is.null(ph_scen[[nm]])) {
        d[, dp_shift := 0]
    } else {
        path <- ph_est[cohort == ph_scen[[nm]], .(dp_cf = mean(dp)), by = age]
        d <- path[d, on = "age"]
        setorder(d, id, age)
        d[, dp_shift := dp_cf - dp][, dp := dp_cf]
    }
    e_p <- predict(ph_prep, newdata = d, type = "link")
    res <- data.table(
        cohort = d[age == 1, cohort],
        truth  = ph_cif60(d$eta_d + ph_mu * d$dp_shift, d$eta_p + 3 * d$dp_shift, d$id),
        naive  = ph_cif60(predict(ph_naive, newdata = d, type = "link"), e_p, d$id),
        cf     = ph_cif60(predict(ph_cf, newdata = d, type = "link"), e_p, d$id))
    res[, .(Truth = 100 * mean(truth), `Naive hazard` = 100 * mean(naive),
            `Control function` = 100 * mean(cf)), by = cohort][, Scenario := nm]
}))
ph_gap <- ph_out[cohort %in% c(2003, 2006),
                 lapply(.SD, diff), by = Scenario,
                 .SDcols = c("Truth", "Naive hazard", "Control function")]

knitr::kable(rbind(
    data.frame(Quantity = "Rise in average monthly default hazard from a 10% price decline (%)",
               t(100 * ph_decline), check.names = FALSE),
    data.frame(Quantity = paste0("2006 minus 2003 five-year default rate, ", tolower(ph_gap$Scenario),
                                 " (pp)"),
               ph_gap[, -1], check.names = FALSE)
), digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
caption = "Counterfactual quantities from the true model, the naive hazard, and the control function hazard. The last two rows hold the price path fixed across cohorts, so the remaining gap is what cohort characteristics explain.")

text:
Anderson-Rubin (AR) test, originally proposed Anderson Rubin (1949), remains one robust inferential tools context instrumental variable estimation, particularly instruments weak endogenous regressors exhibit complex error structures.AR test directly evaluates joint null hypothesis :\[

\]testing whether instruments explain variation residuals \(Y - \beta_0 X\). null, model becomes:\[

AR(\beta_0) \sim \chi^2(q)

n <- 500

u <- rnorm(n)

set.seed(2026)
n_obs <- 1000
n_rep <- 4000
rho   <- 0.15
gam   <- sqrt(rho / (1 - rho))  # confounder loading giving cor(errors) = rho

sim_iv_ols <- function(EF, beta) {
    pi <- sqrt((EF - 1) * (gam^2 + 1) / n_obs)
    out <- matrix(NA_real_, n_rep, 5,
                  dimnames = list(NULL, c("b_iv", "t_iv", "b_ols", "t_ols", "F")))
    for (r in seq_len(n_rep)) {
        z <- rnorm(n_obs); x <- rnorm(n_obs)
        d <- pi * z + gam * x + rnorm(n_obs)
        y <- beta * d + gam * x + rnorm(n_obs)
        szd <- sum(z * d); szz <- sum(z^2); sdd <- sum(d^2)
        b_iv   <- sum(z * y) / szd
        se_iv  <- sqrt(sum((y - b_iv * d)^2) / (n_obs - 1) * szz) / abs(szd)
        b_ols  <- sum(d * y) / sdd
        se_ols <- sqrt(sum((y - b_ols * d)^2) / (n_obs - 1) / sdd)
        pihat  <- szd / szz
        se_pi  <- sqrt(sum((d - pihat * z)^2) / (n_obs - 1) / szz)
        out[r, ] <- c(b_iv, b_iv / se_iv, b_ols, b_ols / se_ols, (pihat / se_pi)^2)
    }
    as.data.frame(out)
}

grid <- expand.grid(EF = c(20, 80, 200), beta = c(0, 0.1))
sims <- Map(sim_iv_ols, grid$EF, grid$beta)

hitl_tab <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(s, EF, beta) {
    sig_iv  <- abs(s$t_iv)  > 1.96
    sig_ols <- abs(s$t_ols) > 1.96
    data.frame(
        `E(F)` = EF, beta = beta,
        `IV, all`          = median(abs(s$b_iv - beta)),
        `IV, significant`  = median(abs(s$b_iv[sig_iv] - beta)),
        `OLS, significant` = median(abs(s$b_ols[sig_ols] - beta)),
        `Share IV significant` = mean(sig_iv),
        check.names = FALSE
    )
}, sims, grid$EF, grid$beta))

knitr::kable(hitl_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Median absolute bias of IV and OLS with and without a significance filter ($\\rho = 0.15$, $n = 1000$).")
s20 <- sims[[which(grid$EF == 20 & grid$beta == 0.1)]]
thresholds <- c(0, 10, 20, 30)
thr_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(thresholds, function(c0) {
    keep <- s20$F > c0 & abs(s20$t_iv) > 1.96
    data.frame(`F threshold` = c0,
               `Median absolute bias` = median(abs(s20$b_iv[keep] - 0.1)),
               `Reported estimates` = sum(keep),
               check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(thr_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Significant IV estimates screened on the realized first-stage F ($E(F) = 20$, $\\beta = 0.1$).")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(AER)        # ivreg for TSLS
})

set.seed(20240515)

# Triangular system: continuous instrument Z, continuous endogenous D,
# outcome Y with a non-linear structural function g(D) = sin(D) + 0.3 D.
n  <- 2000
Z  <- runif(n, -3, 3)                       # instrument
U  <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)                    # structural error
V  <- rnorm(n, sd = 0.5) + 0.6 * U          # first-stage error,
                                            # correlated with U (endogeneity)
D  <- 0.8 * Z + V                           # endogenous treatment
Y  <- sin(D) + 0.3 * D + U                  # non-linear g(D) + error

dat <- data.frame(Y, D, Z)
head(dat)
#>            Y          D           Z
#> 1  1.3088495  1.4660636  1.30894489
#> 2 -0.6194982 -0.6651576 -0.63429301
#> 3  1.4406402  1.6474791  1.24417622
#> 4 -2.0037418 -1.0214914 -0.84389958
#> 5 -0.5200524 -0.5456064 -0.09375499
#> 6  1.3100310  1.2543102  2.38212793
linear_tsls <- ivreg(Y ~ D | Z, data = dat)
summary(linear_tsls)$coefficients
#>                 Estimate  Std. Error    t value Pr(>|t|)
#> (Intercept) -0.004130155 0.013196916 -0.3129636 0.754341
#> D            0.731509921 0.009403496 77.7912734 0.000000
#> attr(,"df")
#> [1] 1998
#> attr(,"nobs")
#> [1] 2000
#> attr(,"logLik")
#> 'log Lik.' -1782.226 (df=3)
# Polynomial TSLS: instrument D and D^2 with Z and Z^2.
dat$D2 <- dat$D^2
dat$Z2 <- dat$Z^2

quad_tsls <- ivreg(Y ~ D + D2 | Z + Z2, data = dat)
summary(quad_tsls)$coefficients
#>                 Estimate  Std. Error    t value  Pr(>|t|)
#> (Intercept)  0.011923801 0.021768450  0.5477561 0.5839206
#> D            0.731784908 0.009409474 77.7710718 0.0000000
#> D2          -0.006960565 0.007505724 -0.9273676 0.3538478
#> attr(,"df")
#> [1] 1997
#> attr(,"nobs")
#> [1] 2000
#> attr(,"logLik")
#> 'log Lik.' -1781.884 (df=4)

# Recover the fitted dose-response on a grid. We compute the prediction
# manually from the fitted coefficients, since AER::predict.ivreg expects
# the instruments in newdata, not just the regressors.
d_grid <- seq(min(dat$D), max(dat$D), length.out = 100)
beta   <- coef(quad_tsls)
quad_curve <- data.frame(
  D      = d_grid,
  Y_hat  = beta["(Intercept)"] + beta["D"] * d_grid + beta["D2"] * d_grid^2,
  Y_true = sin(d_grid) + 0.3 * d_grid
)

ggplot(quad_curve, aes(x = D)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Y_hat), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Y_true), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Endogenous treatment D",
       y = "g(D): structural outcome at dose D",
       title = "Quadratic-TSLS dose-response, by hand",
       subtitle = "Solid: fitted polynomial-TSLS. Dashed red: true g(D).") +
  theme_minimal()

set.seed(1977)
n    <- 4e6
z    <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)                 # high versus low ad exposure
type <- sample(c("always", "complier", "never"), n, replace = TRUE,
               prob = c(0.020, 0.005, 0.975))
d    <- as.integer(type == "always" | (type == "complier" & z == 1))

# Predetermined trait: first-time filer status
first_time <- rbinom(n, 1, c(always = 0.84, complier = 0.93, never = 0.80)[type])
# Post-instrument choice, observed only for filers: hiring a lawyer.
# Ads also nudge always-takers toward a lawyer (+2 points).
lawyer <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(type == "never", 0,
                 c(always = 0.90, complier = 0.97, never = 0)[type] +
                   0.02 * (type == "always") * z))

# Full-data complier mean (needs X for everyone)
complier_mean_full <- function(x) {
  (mean(x[z == 1] * d[z == 1]) - mean(x[z == 0] * d[z == 0])) /
    (mean(d[z == 1]) - mean(d[z == 0]))
}

# Treated-only complier mean: X from the filer records, s from the aggregate first stage
s <- 1 - mean(d[z == 0]) / mean(d[z == 1])
filers <- data.frame(first_time, lawyer, z)[d == 1, ]
complier_mean_treated <- function(var) {
  fit  <- lm(reformulate("z", var), data = filers)
  mu_a <- mean(filers[[var]][filers$z == 0])
  c(estimate = mu_a + coef(fit)[["z"]] / s,
    se       = sqrt(vcov(fit)["z", "z"]) / s)
}

  variable          = c("first_time (predetermined)", "lawyer (post-instrument)"),
  truth             = c(0.93, 0.97),

  full_data_formula = c(complier_mean_full(first_time), NA),
  treated_only      = c(complier_mean_treated("first_time")[["estimate"]],
                        complier_mean_treated("lawyer")[["estimate"]]),
  treated_only_se   = c(complier_mean_treated("first_time")[["se"]],
                        complier_mean_treated("lawyer")[["se"]]),

) |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)

# Load necessary libraries
library(shiny)
library(AER)  # for ivreg
library(ggplot2)  # for visualization
library(dplyr)  # for data manipulation

# Function to simulate the dataset
simulate_iv_data <- function(n, beta, phi, direct_effect) {
  Z <- rnorm(n)
  epsilon_x <- rnorm(n)
  epsilon_y <- rnorm(n)
  X <- phi * Z + epsilon_x
  Y <- beta * X + direct_effect * Z + epsilon_y
  data <- data.frame(Y = Y, X = X, Z = Z)
  return(data)
}

# Function to run the simulations and calculate the effects
run_simulation <- function(n, beta, phi, direct_effect) {
  # Simulate the data
  simulated_data <- simulate_iv_data(n, beta, phi, direct_effect)
  
  # Estimate first-stage effect (phi)
  first_stage <- lm(X ~ Z, data = simulated_data)
  phi <- coef(first_stage)["Z"]
  phi_ci <- confint(first_stage)["Z", ]
  
  # Estimate reduced-form effect (rho)
  reduced_form <- lm(Y ~ Z, data = simulated_data)
  rho <- coef(reduced_form)["Z"]
  rho_ci <- confint(reduced_form)["Z", ]
  
  # Estimate LATE using IV regression
  iv_model <- ivreg(Y ~ X | Z, data = simulated_data)
  iv_late <- coef(iv_model)["X"]
  iv_late_ci <- confint(iv_model)["X", ]
  
  # Calculate LATE as the ratio of reduced-form and first-stage coefficients
  calculated_late <- rho / phi
  calculated_late_se <- sqrt(
    (rho_ci[2] - rho)^2 / phi^2 + (rho * (phi_ci[2] - phi) / phi^2)^2
  )
  calculated_late_ci <- c(calculated_late - 1.96 * calculated_late_se, 
                          calculated_late + 1.96 * calculated_late_se)
  
  # Return a list of results
  list(phi = phi, 
       phi_ci = phi_ci,
       rho = rho, 
       rho_ci = rho_ci,
       direct_effect = direct_effect,
       direct_effect_ci = c(direct_effect, direct_effect),  # Placeholder for direct effect CI
       iv_late = iv_late, 
       iv_late_ci = iv_late_ci,
       calculated_late = calculated_late, 
       calculated_late_ci = calculated_late_ci,
       true_effect = beta,
       true_effect_ci = c(beta, beta))  # Placeholder for true effect CI
}

# Define UI for the sliders
ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("IV Model Simulation"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("beta", "True Effect of X on Y (beta):", min = 0, max = 1.0, value = 0.5, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("phi", "First Stage Effect (phi):", min = 0, max = 1.0, value = 0.7, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("direct_effect", "Direct Effect of Z on Y:", min = -0.5, max = 0.5, value = 0, step = 0.1)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("dotPlot")
    )
  )
)

# Define server logic to run the simulation and generate the plot
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$dotPlot <- renderPlot({
    # Run simulation
    results <- run_simulation(n = 1000, beta = input$beta, phi = input$phi, direct_effect = input$direct_effect)
    
    # Prepare data for plotting
    plot_data <- data.frame(
      Effect = c("First Stage (phi)", "Reduced Form (rho)", "Direct Effect", "LATE (Ratio)", "LATE (IV)", "True Effect"),
      Value = c(results$phi, results$rho, results$direct_effect, results$calculated_late, results$iv_late, results$true_effect),
      CI_Lower = c(results$phi_ci[1], results$rho_ci[1], results$direct_effect_ci[1], results$calculated_late_ci[1], results$iv_late_ci[1], results$true_effect_ci[1]),
      CI_Upper = c(results$phi_ci[2], results$rho_ci[2], results$direct_effect_ci[2], results$calculated_late_ci[2], results$iv_late_ci[2], results$true_effect_ci[2])
    )
    
    # Create dot plot with confidence intervals
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Effect, y = Value)) +
      geom_point(size = 3) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CI_Lower, ymax = CI_Upper), width = 0.2) +
      labs(title = "IV Model Effects",
           y = "Coefficient Value") +
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-1, 1)) +  # Limits the y-axis to -1 to 1 but allows CI beyond
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  })
}

# Run the application 
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

set.seed(2024)
n <- 5000

Z <- rnorm(n)
u <- rnorm(n)                            # the confounder
X <- 0.6 * Z + 0.8 * u + rnorm(n)        # endogenous regressor

beta_true  <- 1
gamma_true <- 0.1                        # small direct effect of Z on Y
Y <- beta_true * X + gamma_true * Z + 0.8 * u + rnorm(n)

demean <- function(v) v - mean(v)
Zc <- demean(Z)
Xc <- demean(X)
Yc <- demean(Y)

b_iv  <- sum(Zc * Yc) / sum(Zc * Xc)
resid <- Yc - b_iv * Xc
se_iv <- sqrt(sum(Zc^2 * resid^2)) / abs(sum(Zc * Xc))   # heteroskedasticity robust
A     <- sum(Zc^2) / sum(Zc * Xc)                        # how hard gamma moves the estimate

crit <- qnorm(0.975)

# union of 95% intervals over |gamma| <= delta
uci <- function(delta) {
  grid <- seq(-delta, delta, length.out = 201)
  centres <- b_iv - A * grid
  c(lower = min(centres) - crit * se_iv,
    upper = max(centres) + crit * se_iv)
}

# local-to-zero interval with gamma ~ N(0, sd_gamma^2)
ltz <- function(sd_gamma) {
  se <- sqrt(se_iv^2 + (A * sd_gamma)^2)
  c(lower = b_iv - crit * se, upper = b_iv + crit * se)
}

deltas <- c(0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
sensitivity <- data.frame(
  gamma_bound = deltas,
  uci_lower   = sapply(deltas, function(d) uci(d)["lower"]),
  uci_upper   = sapply(deltas, function(d) uci(d)["upper"]),
  ltz_lower   = sapply(deltas, function(d) ltz(d)["lower"]),
  ltz_upper   = sapply(deltas, function(d) ltz(d)["upper"])
)

set.seed(11)

sargan_p <- function(y, d, Z) {
  n    <- length(y)
  D    <- cbind(1, d)
  Zf   <- cbind(1, Z)
  Dhat <- Zf %*% qr.solve(Zf, D)
  b    <- qr.solve(Dhat, y)
  u    <- as.vector(y - D %*% b)
  stat <- n * summary(lm(u ~ Z))$r.squared
  pchisq(stat, df = ncol(Z) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

draw_iv <- function(n, heterogeneous, invalid) {
  Z1  <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  Z2  <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  grp <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)            # which instrument a unit responds to
  u   <- rnorm(n)                     # the confounder
  d   <- as.numeric(-0.4 + 1.4 * ifelse(grp == 1, Z1, Z2) + 0.8 * u + rnorm(n) > 0)
  beta <- if (heterogeneous) ifelse(grp == 1, 1, 3) else 2
  y <- beta * d + 0.8 * u + rnorm(n) + if (invalid) 0.35 * Z2 else 0
  list(y = y, d = d, Z = cbind(Z1, Z2))
}

a1 <- 2.0; b1 <- -1.0                # E[Y(1) | U = u] = a1 + b1 * u
a0 <- 0.2; b0 <-  2.0                # E[Y(0) | U = u] = a0 + b0 * u
Y  <- ifelse(D == 1, a1 + b1 * U, a0 + b0 * U) + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)

wald <- function(keep, z) {
  (mean(Y[keep & z == 1]) - mean(Y[keep & z == 0])) /
    (mean(D[keep & z == 1]) - mean(D[keep & z == 0]))
}

observed <- c(
  `Z1 given Z2 = 0` = wald(Z2 == 0, Z1),
  `Z1 given Z2 = 1` = wald(Z2 == 1, Z1),
  `Z2 given Z1 = 0` = wald(Z1 == 0, Z2),
  `Z2 given Z1 = 1` = wald(Z1 == 1, Z2)
)

# nonparametric first stage, then the separate approach to the MTE curve
p_hat <- ave(D, Z1, Z2, FUN = mean)
m1 <- lm(Y ~ p_hat, subset = D == 1)
m0 <- lm(Y ~ p_hat, subset = D == 0)
a1_hat <- coef(m1)[1]
b1_hat <- 2 * coef(m1)[2]
a0_hat <- coef(m0)[1] - coef(m0)[2]
b0_hat <- 2 * coef(m0)[2]

mte_late <- function(pa, pb) (a1_hat - a0_hat) + (b1_hat - b0_hat) * (pa + pb) / 2

margins <- list(c(0.10, 0.35), c(0.55, 0.80), c(0.10, 0.55), c(0.35, 0.80))
data.frame(
  complier_margin = sapply(margins, function(m) paste0("(", m[1], ", ", m[2], "]")),
  wald            = round(as.numeric(observed), 3),
  mte_implied     = round(sapply(margins, function(m) mte_late(m[1], m[2])), 3),
  truth           = round(sapply(margins, function(m) (a1 - a0) + (b1 - b0) * (m[1] + m[2]) / 2), 3)
)

late_range_check <- function(y, d, z) {
  pi_c <- mean(d[z == 1]) - mean(d[z == 0])
  rho  <- mean(y[z == 1]) - mean(y[z == 0])
  c(first_stage = pi_c,
    reduced_form = rho,
    wald = rho / pi_c,
    complier_mean_y1 = (mean((y * d)[z == 1]) - mean((y * d)[z == 0])) / pi_c,
    complier_mean_y0 = (mean((y * (1 - d))[z == 0]) - mean((y * (1 - d))[z == 1])) / pi_c,
    min_direct_effect = max(0, abs(rho) - pi_c))
}

simulate_range <- function(n, direct) {
  z    <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  type <- sample(c("always", "complier", "never"), n, replace = TRUE,
                 prob = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.94))
  d    <- as.integer(type == "always" | (type == "complier" & z == 1))
  # Filing raises the chance of a prime score by 30 points; the instrument
  # also raises it directly for everyone by `direct` (debt renegotiation).
  p    <- 0.35 + 0.30 * d + direct * z
  y    <- rbinom(n, 1, p)
  late_range_check(y, d, z)
}

set.seed(2024)

library(dplyr)
library(fixest)

# 1. Simulate data
N_judges <- 100
N_cases  <- 20000

# Judge-level leniency (propensity to assign treatment D = 1)
judge_leniency <- runif(N_judges, 0.2, 0.8)

# Cases are as-good-as-randomly assigned to judges
cases <- tibble(
    case_id  = 1:N_cases,
    judge_id = sample(1:N_judges, N_cases, replace = TRUE),
    U        = rnorm(N_cases)                    # unobserved confounder
)

cases <- cases |>
    mutate(
        prop = judge_leniency[judge_id],         # judge leniency
        # Treatment depends on the judge AND on U. The latent index has unit
        # variance, so each judge still treats a share `prop` of cases.
        D    = as.integer(qnorm(prop) + 0.8 * U + rnorm(N_cases, sd = 0.6) > 0),
        # True causal effect of treatment = -0.5; U confounds OLS
        Y    = -0.5 * D + 0.8 * U + rnorm(N_cases, sd = 0.5)
    )

# 2. Leave-one-out judge leniency instrument
judge_totals <- cases |>
    group_by(judge_id) |>
    summarise(sum_D = sum(D), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

cases <- cases |>
    left_join(judge_totals, by = "judge_id") |>
    mutate(Z = (sum_D - D) / (n - 1))            # leave-one-out leniency

# 3. OLS is biased; 2SLS on the leniency instrument is consistent
ols <- feols(Y ~ D, data = cases)
iv  <- feols(Y ~ 1 | D ~ Z, data = cases)

# Compare OLS and 2SLS
etable(ols, iv,
       headers  = c("Biased OLS", "Judge-IV (2SLS)"),
       dict     = c(D = "Treatment (D)"),
       fitstat  = ~ n + r2 + ivf)

library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
setFixest_notes(FALSE)

js_beta <- -10                                  # true effect of conversion on recovery

js_simulate <- function(n_dist = 30, n_days = 1500, W = 10, margin = 0.01) {
    # Judges: true conversion propensity theta, observed as a past conversion rate Z
    judges <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_dist), function(d) {
        K <- sample(3:6, 1)
        tibble(district = d, judge = paste0(d, "_", seq_len(K)),
               theta = runif(K, 0.03, 0.30))
    })) |>
        mutate(Z = rbinom(n(), 200, theta) / 200)

    # Cases: size, hedge fund creditor (hf), unsecured hedge fund creditor (uhf),
    # experienced counsel (ec), and unobserved quality U
    cases <- tibble(district = rep(seq_len(n_dist), each = n_days),
                    day0 = rep(seq_len(n_days), n_dist)) |>
        mutate(n = rpois(n(), 3)) |>
        filter(n > 0) |>
        tidyr::uncount(n) |>
        mutate(
            large      = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.15),
            log_assets = ifelse(large == 1, rnorm(n(), 16, 1), rnorm(n(), 12, 1)),
            industry   = sample(1:8, n(), replace = TRUE),
            hf   = rbinom(n(), 1, ifelse(large == 1, 0.16, 0.02)),
            uhf  = hf * rbinom(n(), 1, 0.6),
            ec   = rbinom(n(), 1, ifelse(large == 1, 0.15, 0.02)),
            soph = as.integer(large == 1 & (uhf == 1 | ec == 1)),   # able to shop
            U    = 0.3 * hf + 0.7 * pmax(uhf, ec) + rnorm(n())
        )

    # Assignment within one district. Large cases come from a deck holding each
    # judge once; sophisticated filers wait (up to W days) for a lenient deck.
    assign_district <- function(cd, Zj) {
        J <- seq_along(Zj); zbar <- mean(Zj); n <- nrow(cd)
        jd <- integer(n); fday <- integer(n); mu <- numeric(n)
        deck <- sample(J)
        pending <- which(cd$soph == 1)
        naive_by_day <- split(which(cd$soph == 0), cd$day0[cd$soph == 0])
        for (t in seq_len(n_days + W)) {
            exp_now <- if (length(deck)) mean(Zj[deck]) else zbar
            go <- cd$day0[pending] <= t &
                (exp_now <= zbar - margin | cd$day0[pending] + W <= t)
            today <- c(naive_by_day[[as.character(t)]], pending[go])
            pending <- pending[!go]
            for (i in today[sample.int(length(today))]) {
                fday[i] <- t
                if (cd$large[i] == 1) {
                    if (!length(deck)) deck <- sample(J)
                    mu[i] <- mean(Zj[deck])        # expected Z given the deck
                    k <- if (length(deck) > 1) sample.int(length(deck), 1) else 1L
                    jd[i] <- deck[k]
                    deck <- deck[-k]
                } else {
                    mu[i] <- zbar
                    jd[i] <- sample.int(length(J), 1)
                }
            }
        }
        cd$judge <- paste0(cd$district[1], "_", jd)
        cd$fday <- fday
        cd$mu <- mu
        cd
    }

    cases <- bind_rows(lapply(split(cases, cases$district), function(cd)
        assign_district(cd, judges$Z[judges$district == cd$district[1]]))) |>
        left_join(judges |> select(judge, theta, Z), by = "judge") |>
        mutate(
            year = pmin(ceiling(fday / 250), 6),
            dy   = paste(district, year),                       # assignment cell
            D    = rbinom(n(), 1, pmin(pmax(theta - 0.04 * U, 0.005), 0.95)),
            Y    = 20 + js_beta * D + 8 * U + 5 * large + rnorm(n(), 0, 10),
            Ztil = Z - mu                                       # recentered instrument
        )
    list(cases = cases, judges = judges, n_days = n_days, W = W)
}

set.seed(20261001)
js <- js_simulate()
js_big <- filter(js$cases, large == 1)
c(cases = nrow(js$cases), large = nrow(js_big),
  able_to_shop = sum(js_big$soph), judges = nrow(js$judges))
#>        cases        large able_to_shop       judges 
#>       135203        20068         4679          132
js_ctrl <- "log_assets + i(industry)"

# (1) Conventional balance test: leniency on case characteristics, all cases
js_bal <- feols(as.formula(paste("Z ~ large +", js_ctrl, "| dy")), js$cases,
                cluster = ~judge)

# (2) Leniency on the parties able to shop, large cases; secured HF as benchmark

               cluster = ~judge)

# (3) The assignment rule: does a large case last week predict one this week?
js_week <- js_big |>
    mutate(week = (fday - 1) %/% 5) |>
    count(judge, week, name = "n_large")
js_panel <- tidyr::expand_grid(judge = js$judges$judge,
                               week = 0:((js$n_days + js$W - 1) %/% 5)) |>
    left_join(js_week, by = c("judge", "week")) |>
    mutate(any_large = as.integer(coalesce(n_large, 0L) > 0)) |>
    left_join(js$judges |> select(judge, district), by = "judge") |>
    arrange(judge, week) |>
    group_by(judge) |>
    mutate(lag_any = lag(any_large)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(dy = paste(district, pmin(week %/% 50 + 1, 6)))
js_cons <- feols(any_large ~ lag_any | judge + dy, js_panel, cluster = ~judge)

# Nevo and Rosen (2012) one-sided bound after partialling out controls and cells.
# Valid when rho(Z,U) has the sign of rho(D,U) and |rho(Z,U)| <= |rho(D,U)|.
js_nr_bound <- function(dat, ctrl) {
    r <- resid(feols(as.formula(paste0("c(Y, D, Z) ~ ", ctrl, " | dy")), dat))
    y <- r[, 1]; d <- r[, 2]; z <- r[, 3]
    v <- sd(d) * z - sd(z) * d
    iv <- function(w) cov(w, y) / cov(w, d)
    max(iv(z), iv(v))                      # rho(D,Z) > 0 and rho(D,U) < 0
}

js_estimates <- function(cases) {
    big <- filter(cases, large == 1)
    iv <- function(fml) coef(feols(as.formula(fml), big))[["fit_D"]]
    c(`OLS` = coef(feols(as.formula(paste("Y ~ D +", js_ctrl, "| dy")), big))[["D"]],
      `2SLS, conventional` = iv(paste("Y ~", js_ctrl, "| dy | D ~ Z")),
      `2SLS + hedge fund indicators` = iv(paste("Y ~ uhf + hf +", js_ctrl, "| dy | D ~ Z")),
      `2SLS + all shopping indicators` = iv(paste("Y ~ uhf + hf + ec +", js_ctrl, "| dy | D ~ Z")),
      `2SLS, recentered instrument` = iv(paste("Y ~", js_ctrl, "| dy | D ~ Ztil")),
      `Nevo-Rosen lower bound` = js_nr_bound(big, js_ctrl),
      `Nevo-Rosen lower bound + hedge fund indicators` = js_nr_bound(big, paste("uhf + hf +", js_ctrl)))
}

library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
setFixest_notes(FALSE)

grb_rec <- c(2007 + 11/12, 2009.5)           # NBER dates: Dec 2007 to Jun 2009
grb_in_rec <- function(t) as.integer(t >= grb_rec[1] & t < grb_rec[2])

grb_simulate <- function(n_au = 60, n_exam = 12, per_cell = 30,
                         direct = 0, seed = 2007) {
    set.seed(seed)
    ex <- expand.grid(exam = 1:n_exam, au = 1:n_au)
    ex$speed <- runif(nrow(ex), 0.8, 4.5)        # examiner's historic review time, years

    firms <- expand.grid(k = 1:per_cell, ay = 2002:2009, au = 1:n_au) |>
        mutate(exam   = sample.int(n_exam, n(), replace = TRUE),  # random within art unit
               t_app  = ay + runif(n()),
               docket = runif(n(), 0.1, 0.4),
               q      = rnorm(n()),                               # idea and team quality
               team   = rbinom(n(), 1, plogis(q)),                # observable proxies of q
               pro_se = rbinom(n(), 1, plogis(-1 - q))) |>
        left_join(ex, by = c("au", "exam")) |>
        mutate(t_pred = t_app + docket + speed,                   # predicted decision date
               Z2     = grb_in_rec(t_pred),
               t_act  = t_pred + rnorm(n(), 0, 0.2))

    # Examiners depart from date order in the recession: half of the weak
    # applications due in the year after it are pulled forward into it.
    pull <- with(firms, q < -0.5 & t_act >= grb_rec[2] & t_act < grb_rec[2] + 1 &
                        runif(nrow(firms)) < 0.5)
    firms$t_act[pull] <- runif(sum(pull), grb_rec[1], grb_rec[2])
    firms$Z1 <- grb_in_rec(firms$t_act)

    firms |>
        mutate(
            responsive = rbinom(n(), 1, 0.5),   # launch waits on the patent news
            tau  = 0.12 + 0.10 * rnorm(n()),     # effect of a recession birth on survival
            type = case_when(
                runif(n()) < plogis(-1.8 - 0.8 * q)           ~ "always",   # forced entrepreneurs
                runif(n()) < plogis(-0.3 - 15 * (tau - 0.12)) ~ "never",    # sort on low gains
                TRUE                                           ~ "complier"),
            D = case_when(
                responsive == 0  ~ rbinom(n(), 1, 0.17),  # born years before the news
                type == "always" ~ 1L,
                type == "never"  ~ 0L,
                TRUE             ~ Z1),
            p0 = pmin(pmax(0.62 + 0.12 * q - 0.02 * (speed - 2.6) + 0.03 * (au %% 5), 0.02), 0.98),
            p1 = pmin(pmax(p0 + tau, 0.02), 0.98),
            Y  = rbinom(n(), 1, pmin(ifelse(D == 1, p1, p0) + direct * Z2, 1))  # 7-year survival
        )
}

grb_resp <- filter(grb, responsive == 1)
table(`Actual timing Z1` = grb_resp$Z1, `Predicted timing Z2` = grb_resp$Z2)

#> Actual timing Z1    0    1

grb_fe <- "au^ay"
grb_est <- function(d) {
    r <- filter(d, responsive == 1)
    b <- function(fml, term) coef(feols(as.formula(fml), r))[[term]]
    fs_D  <- b(paste("D ~ Z2 |", grb_fe), "Z2")
    fs_Z1 <- b(paste("Z1 ~ Z2 |", grb_fe), "Z2")
    late  <- with(filter(r, type == "complier"), mean(p1 - p0))
    c(`Naive OLS: Y on D`                  = b(paste("Y ~ D |", grb_fe), "D"),
      `ITT: Y on actual timing Z1`         = b(paste("Y ~ Z1 |", grb_fe), "Z1"),
      `Bias-corrected ITT: Z1 by Z2`       = b(paste("Y ~ 1 |", grb_fe, "| Z1 ~ Z2"), "fit_Z1"),
      `LATE: D by Z2`                      = b(paste("Y ~ 1 |", grb_fe, "| D ~ Z2"), "fit_D"),
      `LATE: D by Z2, examiner speed control` = b(paste("Y ~ speed |", grb_fe, "| D ~ Z2"), "fit_D"),
      `True bias-corrected ITT`            = late * fs_D / fs_Z1,
      `True LATE (compliers)`              = late)
}

set.seed(2026)
n <- 50000

# Unobserved activity shock: drives both viewing time and baseline demand
u <- rnorm(n)

# Household watches a contiguous window of the (unit-length) show.
# Longer windows for high-activity households, truncated to [0.05, 1].
len <- pmin(pmax(0.35 + 0.15 * u + 0.2 * runif(n), 0.05), 1)
start <- runif(n) * (1 - len)

# Network airs the ad at a quasi-random time, common density (uniform here),
# independent of households and of the brand's targeting.
ad_time <- runif(n)

# Exposure: ad time falls inside the watched window
A <- as.numeric(ad_time >= start & ad_time <= start + len)

# Exposure probability given viewing (uniform density: the window length),
# and the timing instrument
P <- len
IV <- A - P

# Purchase intensity: true ad effect 0.10, activity confounding through u
Y <- 0.10 * A + 0.25 * u + rnorm(n)

naive <- coef(lm(Y ~ A))["A"]
iv_est <- coef(ivreg::ivreg(Y ~ A | IV))["A"]

# Control-function variant: include the first-stage residual
cf_res <- resid(lm(A ~ IV))
cf_est <- coef(lm(Y ~ A + cf_res))["A"]

round(c(naive = naive, iv = iv_est, control_fn = cf_est), 4)
#>      naive.A         iv.A control_fn.A

library(fixest)
set.seed(101)

sim_elig <- function(policy_endog = 0) {
  S <- 50; Tt <- 10
  g <- expand.grid(state = 1:S, year = 1:Tt)
  n <- nrow(g)
  # Composition varies WITHIN state over time, so state fixed effects cannot
  # absorb it. This is the confound the simulated instrument is built to remove.
  comp <- rnorm(S)[g$state] + rnorm(n)
  rule <- rnorm(n) + policy_endog * comp        # statutory generosity
  elig_actual <- 0.5 * rule + 0.8 * comp + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)
  elig_sim    <- 0.5 * rule                     # rule on a FIXED national sample
  y <- 1.0 * elig_actual + 1.5 * comp + rnorm(n)

  d <- data.frame(y, elig_actual, elig_sim,
                  state = factor(g$state), year = factor(g$year))
  c(ols = unname(coef(feols(y ~ elig_actual | state + year, data = d))[1]),
    siv = unname(coef(feols(y ~ 1 | state + year | elig_actual ~ elig_sim,
                            data = d))["fit_elig_actual"]))
}

res <- t(sapply(c(0, 0.5, 1.0), function(pe)
  c(policy_endogeneity = pe, round(rowMeans(replicate(150, sim_elig(pe))), 3))))
knitr::kable(res, row.names = FALSE,

set.seed(404)

mr_once <- function(J = 40, regime = "none", frac = 0.4, beta = 0.3) {
  gam <- runif(J, 0.05, 0.20)                       # variant -> exposure
  alpha <- switch(regime,
    none        = rep(0, J),
    balanced    = rnorm(J, 0, 0.03),                # mean-zero pleiotropy
    directional = { a <- rep(0, J)
                    a[seq_len(round(frac * J))] <-
                      abs(rnorm(round(frac * J), 0.04, 0.01)); a })
  Gam  <- alpha + beta * gam                        # variant -> outcome
  se_g <- rep(0.01, J); se_G <- rep(0.015, J)
  gh <- gam + rnorm(J, 0, se_g)                     # published estimates
  Gh  <- Gam + rnorm(J, 0, se_G)

  w <- 1 / se_G^2
  ivw <- sum(w * gh * Gh) / sum(w * gh^2)           # inverse-variance weighted
  eg  <- coef(lm(Gh ~ gh, weights = w))             # MR-Egger
  ratio <- Gh / gh; se_r <- se_G / abs(gh)          # weighted median
  o <- order(ratio)
  cw <- cumsum((1 / se_r^2)[o]) / sum(1 / se_r^2)
  c(IVW = ivw, Egger_slope = unname(eg[2]), Egger_intercept = unname(eg[1]),
    Weighted_median = ratio[o][which.min(abs(cw - 0.5))])
}

tab <- t(sapply(c("none", "balanced", "directional"), function(r)
  round(rowMeans(replicate(300, mr_once(regime = r))), 4)))

                  "pleiotropy regimes. The true causal effect is 0.300."))

set.seed(202)

km <- function(nf = 800, nb = 60) {
  bshock <- rnorm(nb)                    # bank liquidity shock
  brank  <- order(bshock)
  fdem   <- rnorm(nf)                    # firm credit demand, unobserved
  # Assortative matching: firms with strong demand borrow from healthier banks.
  # This is what contaminates the cross-sectional comparison.
  pick <- function() {
    i <- round(rank(fdem) / nf * nb + rnorm(nf, 0, 8))
    brank[pmin(pmax(i, 1), nb)]
  }
  b1 <- pick(); b2 <- pick()
  keep <- b1 != b2
  b1 <- b1[keep]; b2 <- b2[keep]; fd <- fdem[keep]; n <- length(b1)

  L1 <- 0.8 * bshock[b1] + fd + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)   # true supply effect = 0.8
  L2 <- 0.8 * bshock[b2] + fd + rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)

  long <- data.frame(L = c(L1, L2), shock = c(bshock[b1], bshock[b2]))
  c(cross_sectional = unname(coef(lm(L ~ shock, data = long))["shock"]),
    within_borrower = unname(coef(lm(I(L1 - L2) ~
                                       I(bshock[b1] - bshock[b2])))[2]))

set.seed(123)
n  <- 5000
x1 <- rnorm(n)
x2 <- rnorm(n)
x3 <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4)

# Confounded assignment and outcomes, true ATE = 1
e_true <- plogis(-0.5 + 0.8 * x1 - 0.6 * x2 + 0.4 * x3)
d  <- rbinom(n, 1, e_true)
y0 <- 2 + 1.0 * x1 + 0.5 * x2 + 0.3 * x3 + rnorm(n)
y  <- ifelse(d == 1, y0 + 1, y0)
dat <- data.frame(y, d, x1, x2, x3)

ps_fit <- glm(d ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = dat, family = binomial())
e_hat  <- fitted(ps_fit)

ate_naive <- mean(dat$y[dat$d == 1]) - mean(dat$y[dat$d == 0])
ate_reg   <- coef(lm(y ~ d + x1 + x2 + x3, data = dat))["d"]

# ATE weights (Horvitz-Thompson)
w_ipw <- ifelse(dat$d == 1, 1 / e_hat, 1 / (1 - e_hat))
ate_ipw <- weighted.mean(dat$y[dat$d == 1], w_ipw[dat$d == 1]) -
    weighted.mean(dat$y[dat$d == 0], w_ipw[dat$d == 0])

# Overlap weights
w_ow <- ifelse(dat$d == 1, 1 - e_hat, e_hat)
ate_ow <- weighted.mean(dat$y[dat$d == 1], w_ow[dat$d == 1]) -
    weighted.mean(dat$y[dat$d == 0], w_ow[dat$d == 0])

ess <- function(w) sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)

data.frame(
    estimator = c("Naive", "Regression", "IPW (ATE)", "Overlap"),
    estimate  = round(c(ate_naive, ate_reg, ate_ipw, ate_ow), 3),
    ess_controls = round(c(NA, NA, ess(w_ipw[dat$d == 0]),
                           ess(w_ow[dat$d == 0])))
)

\delta_{TOT} &= E [ E[ Y_{1i} | X_i, D_i = 1] - E[ Y_{0i}|X_i, D_i = 0 ]|D_i = 1 ] \\
&= E\left[ E[Y_i \mid X_i, D_i = 1] - E[Y_i \mid X_i, D_i = 0] \mid D_i = 1 \right] \\
&= E[\delta_X |D_i = 1]
\end{aligned}
\]\(\delta_X\) \(X\)-specific difference means covariate value \(X_i\)\(X_i\) discrete, matching estimand becomes:\[
\delta_M = \sum_x \delta_x P(X_i = x \mid D_i = 1)
\]\(P(X_i = x |D_i = 1)\) probability mass function \(X_i\) given \(D_i = 1\)Bayes’ rule:\[
P(X_i = x \mid D_i = 1) = \frac{P(D_i = 1 \mid X_i = x) P(X_i = x)}{P(D_i = 1)}
\],\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta_M &= \frac{\sum_x \delta_x P (D_i = 1 | X_i = x) P (X_i = x)}{\sum_x P(D_i = 1 |X_i = x)P(X_i = x)} \\
&= \sum_x \delta_x \frac{ P (D_i = 1 | X_i = x) P (X_i = x)}{\sum_x P(D_i = 1 |X_i = x)P(X_i = x)}
\end{aligned}
\]

library(Matching)
data(lalonde, package = "MatchIt")
attach(lalonde)

# Define the covariates to match on
X <- cbind(age, educ, black, hisp, married, nodegr, u74, u75, re75, re74)

# Define the covariates to balance on
BalanceMat <- cbind(
  age, educ, black, hisp, married, nodegr,
  u74, u75, re75, re74,
  I(re74 * re75) # Include interaction term
)

# Genetic Matching to optimize covariate balance
# Note: pop.size = 16 is too small for real applications
genout <- GenMatch(
  Tr = treat,
  X = X,
  BalanceMatrix = BalanceMat,
  estimand = "ATE",
  M = 1,
  pop.size = 16,
  max.generations = 10,
  wait.generations = 1
)

# Define the outcome variable
Y <- re78 / 1000

# Perform matching with the optimized weights
mout <- Match(
  Y = Y,
  Tr = treat,
  X = X,
  estimand = "ATE",
  Weight.matrix = genout
)

# Summarize the treatment effect estimates
summary(mout)

# Assess post-matching balance
mb <- MatchBalance(
  treat ~ age + educ + black + hisp + married + nodegr +
    u74 + u75 + re75 + re74 + I(re74 * re75),
  match.out = mout,
  nboots = 500
)

# Load required libraries
library(MatchIt)
library(cobalt)  # For balance checking

# Example dataset: Simulated
set.seed(123)
n <- 400
df <- data.frame(
  treat = factor(sample(c("control", "A", "B", "C"), n, replace = TRUE)),

  cov2 = runif(n),
  cov3 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
  outcome = rnorm(n)
)

# Define treatment levels
treatment_levels <- c("A", "B", "C")
control_level <- "control"

# Initialize weight column
df$match.weights <- 0

# Perform pairwise matching of each treatment group vs control
for (treat in treatment_levels) {
  # Subset to control and current treatment
  subset_df <- df[df$treat %in% c(treat, control_level), ]
  
  # Create a binary treatment variable: 1 for current treatment, 0 for control
  subset_df$treat_binary <- as.numeric(subset_df$treat == treat)

  # Run matching

                   data = subset_df, method = "nearest")

  # Assign weights back to the original dataset
  matched_units <- names(m.out$weights[m.out$weights > 0])
  df[matched_units, "match.weights"] <- m.out$weights[matched_units]

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(tidyr)
})

set.seed(20240515)

# Generate synthetic data: continuous treatment D depends on three
# confounders X1, X2, X3. The true dose-response is quadratic in D
# with a maximum near D = 2 (an inverse-U pattern, common in training
# programmes).
n <- 2000
X1 <- rnorm(n)
X2 <- rnorm(n)
X3 <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.4)

# Treatment-assignment model: D ~ Normal( mu(X), sigma^2 ).
mu_D    <- 1.5 + 0.6 * X1 - 0.4 * X2 + 0.5 * X3
sigma_D <- 1.0
D       <- rnorm(n, mu_D, sigma_D)

# Outcome model: quadratic in D, with confounding via X.
Y <- 0.3 + 1.2 * D - 0.3 * D^2 + 0.5 * X1 + 0.2 * X2 - 0.1 * X3 +
     rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)

dat <- data.frame(Y, D, X1, X2, X3)
head(dat)
#>           Y          D          X1          X2 X3
#> 1  1.230092  2.1599879  0.57737666 -1.15345217  0
#> 2  1.222963  0.7854613  0.54569647 -0.37654112  0
#> 3  1.614434  1.7445367 -0.03917816  0.62338446  1
#> 4  1.798470  1.4843060  1.07327193 -0.04591857  0
#> 5 -1.625341 -0.4028663 -2.06053669  0.56727904  0
#> 6  2.231506  2.2999686  2.45091808  0.56453003  0
# Step 1: fit the conditional mean of D given X.
gps_mean_model <- lm(D ~ X1 + X2 + X3, data = dat)
mu_hat         <- predict(gps_mean_model)
sigma_hat      <- sd(residuals(gps_mean_model))

# GPS = f_{D|X}(D | X), evaluated at the actual treatment.
dat$R <- dnorm(dat$D, mean = mu_hat, sd = sigma_hat)
summary(dat$R)
#>     Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max. 
#> 0.001138 0.203811 0.314014 0.278125 0.371811 0.393358
dat$R_quint <- ntile(dat$R, 5)

balance_check <- dat %>%
  group_by(R_quint) %>%
  summarise(
    cor_D_X1 = cor(D, X1),
    cor_D_X2 = cor(D, X2),
    cor_D_X3 = cor(D, X3),
    n        = n()
  )

# For comparison, the raw correlations before adjustment:

  R_quint  = "RAW (no adjustment)",
  cor_D_X1 = cor(dat$D, dat$X1),
  cor_D_X2 = cor(dat$D, dat$X2),
  cor_D_X3 = cor(dat$D, dat$X3),
  n        = nrow(dat)
)

bind_rows(raw_cor, mutate(balance_check, R_quint = as.character(R_quint)))

#> R           -1.4878512 0.775637020  -1.9182313  5.522435e-02
#> I(R^2)       1.0157479 1.508364331   0.6734102  5.007644e-01
#> D:R          0.6888658 0.101171590   6.8088859  1.297181e-11
d_grid <- seq(min(dat$D), max(dat$D), length.out = 100)

# For each grid value of D, predict the outcome at every unit holding D
# fixed at the grid value (and recomputing the GPS at the counterfactual
# dose), then average over the empirical covariate distribution. The mean
# of the predictions IS the dose-response value at that dose.
dose_response <- sapply(d_grid, function(d_val) {
  r_at_d <- dnorm(d_val, mean = mu_hat, sd = sigma_hat)
  preds  <- predict(outcome_model,
                    newdata = data.frame(D = d_val, R = r_at_d))
  mean(preds)
})

curve_df <- data.frame(
  D      = d_grid,
  Y_hat  = dose_response,
  Y_true = 0.3 + 1.2 * d_grid - 0.3 * d_grid^2
)

ggplot(curve_df, aes(x = D)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Y_hat), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Y_true), linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Dose D",
       y = "E[Y(d)]: average potential outcome at dose d",
       title = "GPS dose-response (Hirano-Imbens two-step, by hand)",
       subtitle = "Solid: fitted dose-response. Dashed red: true curve.") +
  theme_minimal()

code:
# install.packages("CausalGPS")  # CRAN, Khoshnevis, Wu, Braun
library(CausalGPS)

set.seed(20240515)

# Synthetic data: continuous exposure w, six confounders, outcome Y
m_d <- generate_syn_data(sample_size = 1000)
head(m_d)

# Step 1: Estimate the generalized propensity score.
# Here a gradient-boosted (XGBoost) density model is used, with a normal
# density assumption for the conditional distribution of the exposure.
gps_obj <- estimate_gps(
  .data       = m_d,
  .formula    = w ~ I(cf1^2) + cf2 + I(cf3^2) + cf4 + cf5 + cf6,
  sl_lib      = c("m_xgboost"),
  gps_density = "normal"
)

# Step 2: Compute matching weights. The matching is performed in the
# (exposure, GPS) space using L1 distance; delta_n controls the
# exposure-side bandwidth, scale balances exposure vs. GPS proximity.
cw_object <- compute_counter_weight(
  gps_obj      = gps_obj,
  ci_appr      = "matching",
  delta_n      = 0.1,
  dist_measure = "l1",
  scale        = 0.5
)

# Step 3: Build the pseudo-population (each row carries a counter weight
# representing how many units like it would appear in the rebalanced
# population at the dose it actually received).
pseudo_pop <- generate_pseudo_pop(
  .data               = m_d,
  cw_obj              = cw_object,
  covariate_col_names = c("cf1", "cf2", "cf3", "cf4", "cf5", "cf6")
)

# Step 4: Estimate the exposure-response curve at a grid of dose values.
erf_obj <- estimate_erf(
  .data           = pseudo_pop$.data,
  .formula        = Y ~ w,
  weights_col_name = "counter_weight",
  model_type      = "nonparametric",
  w_vals          = seq(2, 20, 0.5),
  kernel_appr     = "kernsmooth"
)

plot(erf_obj)
cw_weight <- compute_counter_weight(
  gps_obj = gps_obj,
  ci_appr = "weighting"
)

library(tidyverse)

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")

# create race dummies if needed

  lalonde <- lalonde %>% mutate(
    black  = as.integer(race == "black"),
    hispan = as.integer(race == "hispanic")
  )
}

# nodegree naming patch
if (!("nodegr" %in% names(lalonde))) {
  if ("nodegree" %in% names(lalonde)) {
    lalonde <- lalonde %>% rename(nodegr = nodegree)
  }
}

# assure 0/1 indicators
lalonde <-
    lalonde %>% mutate(across(c(treat, black, hispan, married, nodegr),
                              as.numeric))

## analysis sample & R^2
vars <- c(
    "log_re78",
    "treat",
    "age",
    "educ",
    "black",
    "hispan",
    "married",
    "nodegr",
    "re74",
    "re75"
)
model_df <- lalonde %>% dplyr::select(all_of(vars)) %>% na.omit()

R2_med <- summary(
    lm(
        log_re78 ~ treat + age + educ + black + hispan +
            married + nodegr + re74 + re75,
        data = model_df
    )
)$r.squared
R2_max <- 1.3 * R2_med # Oster default upper bound

## β* (δ = 1) & δ* (β = 0)

    y = "log_re78",
    x = "treat",
    con = "age + educ + black + hispan + married + nodegr + re74 + re75",

    type = "lm",

    y = "log_re78",
    x = "treat",

set.seed(123)

n <- 2000
p <- 10
X <- matrix(runif(n * p), n, p)

# Nonlinear confounding for both treatment and outcome
g0 <- function(X) sin(2 * pi * X[, 1]) + X[, 2]^2 + 0.5 * X[, 3]
m0 <- function(X) plogis(1.5 * X[, 1] - X[, 2])

theta_true <- 1.0
W <- m0(X) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)          # continuous treatment
Y <- theta_true * W + g0(X) + rnorm(n, sd = 1)

dat <- data.frame(Y = Y, W = W, X)

# Naive plug-in: estimate g on full data, regress residual on W
naive_fit <- lm(Y ~ poly(X1, 3) + poly(X2, 3) + X3, data = dat)
resid_Y <- dat$Y - predict(naive_fit)
theta_naive <- coef(lm(resid_Y ~ dat$W - 1))

# Cross-fitted orthogonal (partialling-out) estimator
K <- 5
folds <- sample(rep(1:K, length.out = n))
vY <- numeric(n); vW <- numeric(n)
for (k in 1:K) {
    tr <- folds != k
    te <- folds == k
    gY <- lm(Y ~ poly(X1, 3) + poly(X2, 3) + X3, data = dat[tr, ])
    gW <- lm(W ~ poly(X1, 3) + poly(X2, 3) + X3, data = dat[tr, ])
    vY[te] <- dat$Y[te] - predict(gY, newdata = dat[te, ])
    vW[te] <- dat$W[te] - predict(gW, newdata = dat[te, ])
}
theta_dml <- sum(vW * vY) / sum(vW * vW)

c(naive = theta_naive, dml = theta_dml, truth = theta_true)

library(DoubleML)

flex <- model.matrix(
    ~ 0 + poly(age, 2, raw = TRUE) + poly(inc, 2, raw = TRUE) +
        poly(educ, 2, raw = TRUE) + poly(fsize, 2, raw = TRUE) +
